label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa contra gentiles I.13 -: The first mover that the argument from motion must…
locator: I.13 [21]-[24]: it yet does not follow that this mover is absolutely unmoved
interpretation: After the second way concludes to a first mover 'not moved by any exterior moving cause' ([20]), Aquinas says this does not yet show it is absolutely unmoved ([21]); for a self-mover one part must be unmoved ([22]-[23]), and since the moving part of animals is moved by accident, Aristotle shows that the moving part of the first self-mover is moved 'neither through itself nor by accident' ([24]-[26]). Read as: the argument from motion is not finished at a mover unmoved in some respect or relative to its series; it must reach a mover moved in no way. This is interpretive evidence that Aquinas does not accept a merely relative first mover, which is what the weaker per se reading of ST I q.2 a.3 yields. The reasoning in [24]-[26] relies on Aristotle's supposition of everlasting motion, which Aquinas discusses in [29]-[30]. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
